_methodology.note: Cappadocia, Gaziantep and Pamukkale are inland — honest distances are given rather than stretching the definition of 'nearby'. Antalya and Bodrum are themselves coastal so their beaches are effectively in-town.

beaches.name: Büyükada (Princes' Islands)
beaches.distanceFromCenter: ~45-55 min by fast ferry from Eminönü/Kabataş
beaches.description: Largest of the car-free Princes' Islands — small rocky/pebble coves rather than a big sandy stretch, but the pine-forest, horse-drawn-carriage atmosphere makes the trip worthwhile beyond just swimming.

beaches.name: Kilyos
beaches.description: Istanbul's main sandy-beach escape — wide shore, beach clubs (Solar, Suma) with a party atmosphere on weekends. Black Sea water is colder and rougher than the Marmara side, with real currents worth respecting.

beaches.name: Florya
beaches.description: The closest beach option to central Istanbul, on the calmer Sea of Marmara — a quick, low-commitment swim rather than a full beach day.

cappadocia.note: Landlocked — nearest coast (Mediterranean via Antalya, or Aegean) is 3-4+ hours by road. Not a realistic beach day trip from here; pair a coastal leg elsewhere in the itinerary instead.

gaziantep.note: Inland — nearest coast (Mediterranean around İskenderun/Hatay) is roughly 2 hours by road. Doable as a stretch day trip but not genuinely 'nearby'.

pamukkale.note: Inland — nearest Aegean coast (Kuşadası area) is roughly 2 hours by road. The Antique travertine pools themselves are the closest thing to a 'swim' here.

beaches.name: Pamucak Beach
beaches.distanceFromCenter: ~15-20 min from Selçuk, ~20 min from Kuşadası
beaches.description: Wide, dark-golden sand backing directly onto the Aegean, and the closest real beach to the Ephesus ruins — genuinely easy to combine a ruins morning with a beach afternoon.

beaches.name: Ladies Beach (Kadınlar Denizi), Kuşadası
beaches.description: Kuşadası's most popular in-town beach — sandy, calm, and lined with cafes, though it gets crowded in peak summer.

beaches.name: Gümbet
beaches.description: The liveliest beach on the peninsula — watersports and a busy bar strip, sandy shore.

beaches.name: Gümüşlük
beaches.description: Quieter, more low-key end of the peninsula — small coves, sunset seafood restaurants, and the submerged ruins of ancient Myndos just offshore.

beaches.name: Ortakent Yalısı
beaches.description: Longer sandy stretch, more residential and relaxed than Gümbet — good middle-ground option for a group wanting space rather than a club scene.

beaches.name: Konyaaltı
beaches.description: Long pebble beach with a dramatic backdrop of the Beydağları mountains — promenade lined with cafes and a beach park.

beaches.name: Lara Beach
beaches.description: Antalya's main sandy beach (Konyaaltı is pebble), backed by the resort strip — the go-to if the group wants actual sand underfoot.

beaches.name: Phaselis
beaches.description: A genuine two-for-one: swim in a small bay directly beside the ruins of an ancient Lycian harbour city, pine forest right down to the water.
